name: Battle of Poltava
note: North is drawn at the top because the Russian camp lay north of Poltava and the Yakovetski woods lay to the east of the Swedish attack. The accounts do not say exactly where either wood lay, so the Budyschenski wood is placed to the south-west, where the Swedes escaped, and the Yakovetski wood to the east. The ten redoubts are drawn as one block. The plan moves the fighting west of the Russian camp as the accounts say, but the distances are not to scale. The accounts give the date in the Gregorian calendar as 8 July 1709 and the hours by the Swedish calendar.

terrain.name: Yakovetski wood
terrain.quote: Roos led the remaining 1,500 of his original 2,600 men into the Yakovetski woods to the east at 6:00 a.m.

terrain.name: Budyschenski wood
terrain.quote: managed to break through and escape to the south through the Budyschenski woods

terrain.name: Poltava
terrain.quote: laid siege to the Russian fortress at Poltava on the Vorskla River on 2 May 1709

units.name: Russian redoubts (4,000 men)
units.quote: 4,000 Russians manned the remaining eight, with 10,000 cavalry under General Aleksandr Danilovich Menshikov stationed behind them

units.name: Menshikov's cavalry
units.quote: 10,000 cavalry under General Aleksandr Danilovich Menshikov stationed behind them

units.name: Russian fortified camp
units.quote: Peter built a fortified camp on the Vorskla, 4 km north of Poltava

units.name: Russian ten regiments
units.quote: launched a two-pronged attack by ten regiments around 7:00 a.m.

units.name: Russian infantry
units.quote: Peter led the 42 battalions of Russian infantry

units.name: Russian dragoons, right
units.quote: Ten regiments of dragoons formed under Lieutenant General Adolf Fredrik Bauer on the Russian right

units.name: Roos' six battalions
units.quote: General Roos and six battalions (one-third of the Swedish infantry) became isolated

units.name: Lewenhaupt's infantry
units.quote: Lewenhaupt's ten battalions on the right bypassed the first four redoubts entirely

units.name: Swedish left-flank infantry
units.quote: the Swedish infantry on the left flank lagged behind the right

units.name: Swedish left-wing cavalry
units.quote: The cavalry on the left wing, commanded by Major General Hamilton

units.name: Creutz's cavalry
units.quote: the cavalry under Major General Carl Gustaf Creutz in the rear

phases.title: The Swedes form south of the redoubts
phases.text: The Swedish columns formed in the night 600 metres south of the redoubts, with the Russian cavalry behind the redoubts and the camp beyond. The infantry was in place early, but the cavalry arrived late.
phases.quote: Four columns of infantry and six columns of cavalry were to form during the night, 600 meters south of the redoubts

phases.title: The Swedish wings pass the redoubts
phases.text: Roos' column overran the first two redoubts but stalled at the third. Lewenhaupt's battalions on the right and Hamilton's cavalry on the left went past the redoubts, and the Russian cavalry retreated.
phases.quote: The cavalry on the left wing, commanded by Major General Hamilton and an infantry regiment, advanced by passing the redoubts on the left and charged the Russian cavalry, forcing them to retreat.

phases.title: Lewenhaupt withdraws west and Roos is cut off
phases.text: Rehnskiöld stopped the pursuit and ordered Lewenhaupt to withdraw to the west, where the wings waited for Roos' battalions. Roos led his remaining 1,500 men into the Yakovetski woods to the east.
phases.quote: Rehnskiöld ordered his cavalry to stop their pursuit and Lewenhaupt, already advancing towards the fort, to withdraw to the west.

phases.title: Roos is driven back and surrenders
phases.text: The Russians retook the first two redoubts and attacked Roos with ten regiments. He fell back towards Poltava, took refuge in an abandoned fort and surrendered at 9:30 a.m.
phases.quote: The Russians reoccupied the first two redoubts and launched a two-pronged attack by ten regiments around 7:00 a.m., forcing Roos to retreat towards Poltava

phases.title: Peter advances and the Swedish line moves forward
phases.text: Peter led his infantry out of the camp, with dragoons on his right and Menshikov's cavalry on his left. Rehnskiöld ordered Lewenhaupt and the Swedish line forward, and the Russian first line retreated towards its second line.
phases.quote: At 09:45, Rehnskiöld ordered Lewenhaupt and the Swedish line to move forward, advancing towards the Russian line

phases.title: The Swedish left flank breaks
phases.text: The Russian line was longer, and the Swedish infantry on the left flank threw down their weapons and fled. A gap opened in the Swedish line, the Russians filled it, and Menshikov's cavalry attacked the Swedes from the rear.
phases.quote: With the Russian line longer than the Swedish line, the Swedish infantry on the left flank lagged behind the right and finally threw down their weapons and fled.

phases.title: The Swedish assault disintegrates
phases.text: Small groups of Swedes broke through and escaped to the south through the Budyschenski woods, while many of the rest were overwhelmed, ridden down or captured. Charles ordered a retreat to the woods with what forces he could gather.
phases.quote: Small groups of soldiers managed to break through and escape to the south through the Budyschenski woods, while many of the rest were overwhelmed, ridden down or captured.
